why: Named compound, direct: 'has a leather-like, phenolic and ink-like odor'. 'ink-like' has no ontology entry. 'part of the cardboard odor' is a separate, composite claim and is not used.
Same sentence as n=321 in a second patent (they differ by one space, so dedupe did not merge them). Valid row, SAME MOLECULE — no gain to leather.
'The woody note' is anaphora and Iso E Super is a comparison; the grapefruit/rooty/vetiver notes belong to the unnamed compound of the invention.
'X can impart a clean note' — the form REVIEW-RULES keeps. clean is at 4 and needs 26.
A statement about what WO 2010/086313 does NOT teach. Not an odour attribution.
Same — absence of teaching in a cited document.
Claim language, 'Use of X to impart a clean note'. Valid, but same molecule and tag as n=413.
'clean linen note' — clean taken from inside it. Same molecule again.
'unusual' is a judgement, not a descriptor; 'etc.' leaves the list open; menthol is the solute.
Named definite compound, 'which imparts lactonic, sage and lavender notes'. lactonic and sage have no ontology entry yet — they land in the unmapped list, which is where candidates belong.
GC-Sniff descriptors belong to an unnamed compound in a spectral block; 4-cyclohexylbutan-2-one is the heading of the NEXT example. A sentence-boundary artefact.
Named, direct: 'having a fine and fruit-like odor'. 'fine' is judgement.
*** PHANTOM RISK *** Same molecule as n=489, scanned with a letter l for the digit 1. A valid row, but approving BOTH gives fruity two spellings of one compound. Decide which one you want.
Named, direct. The space in '7- methyl' is in the source; recorded verbatim.
*** PHANTOM RISK *** Same molecule as n=494, clean spelling. Same choice as the pair above.
'The compounds of the present invention' is a family; the named naphthalene is a TENACITY comparison, and 'synthetic musk' labels its class rather than attributing an odour.
Odour attributed to the isolated compound. peppermint/geranium/caraway are plants — descriptors under the substance-vs-source rule. Name is OCR-damaged ('pmenthan').
*** PHANTOM RISK *** Same molecule as n=567, clean spelling.
Formulation table. The lavender note belongs to the composition.
Same formulation table in a second patent.
THREE compounds sharing ONE description — REVIEW-RULES: add all, approve once. Names are heavily OCR-damaged and recorded verbatim; linkage will have to repair them.
'carbomethoxy-SUBSTITUTED 1,4-dimethyl-bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-5-ene' — substituted X is a family, position unspecified. Mahogonate is a trade name.
Same Mahogonate boilerplate, second patent.
Same Mahogonate boilerplate, third patent.
Same Mahogonate boilerplate, fourth patent.
Same Mahogonate boilerplate, fifth patent.
'This compound' — anaphora.
'The novel compound' — anaphora.
A likeness between thujone and a cyclohexenone. No descriptor is asserted of either.
'a new composition possessing' — composition-level.
'The lime note ... is PROVIDED BY a hydrocarbon ... characterized as X' — the note originates in X. lime is at 2 and needs 28.
'The detergents all possess' — composition-level.
'(iso)propenyl' and 'methanol(s)' with 'and/or' leave the compound indefinite — a family.
Comparative, and the character belongs to the flavour, not the ester.
Named compound, colon, description. 'very natural' is intensity plus judgement.
Isomeric MIXTURE, and the note belongs to the composition.
'an isomer mixture of' — the mixture rule. '4(5)-acetyl' and '(7,9,9)' are alternatives, so the compound is indefinite twice over.
'ketone 8' — numbered anaphora; 16-androstene-3-one is the comparison.
'It further possesses' — anaphora; Cashmeran is the comparison.
Blend effect — 'enhanced by the addition of'.
'Its note' is anaphora and the sentence NEGATES the hay character. Capturing it would assert the opposite.
Full stereodescriptors, so the compound is specific — REVIEW-RULES keeps these. Direct attribution. hay is at 11 and needs 19.
'such as' leaves the list open, and the sulphur note is of grapefruit-type flavours generally. Sentence is cut mid-citation.
Stereodescriptor-specific, direct: 'possesses a herbaceous odor note'. 'less thujonic and drier' is comparative and inverts.
The notes belong to dihydromyrcenol, the comparison, and are conferred on compositions.
Table-row description of a named compound. 'chemical' is a class judgement, 'clay' has no ontology entry. Leading '2 2 2 2' is table garbage. oily is at 9 and needs 21.
